note: FR-FACT-3's rise and set reference, fetched 2026-11-04 in P10's session (V214-19, V214-23). Geometric horizon crossings (no refraction, the body's centre at 0°) over Bariloche on the night of 2026-01-15 (ART, UTC-3), to the minute. JPL Horizons has no stars, so Sirius comes from the US Naval Observatory's celestial-navigation API: its computed altitude `hc` (apparent place, before refraction) sampled each minute, the API drops a star below about 1°, so the crossing is a straight-line fit over the ten minutes nearest the horizon (0.18° a minute, linear to 0.001°). The planet and the Moon are Horizons' own rise and set (`R_T_S_ONLY`, `APPARENT=AIRLESS`, `TVH` at 0°). Never edit by hand.
